text: On the ethics_justice testbed, we evaluated an auxiliary confidence loss on the strong student with an auxiliary loss weight of 0.25, measuring a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.48 with a standard error of 0.17 across num_seeds = 3 seeds. No baseline PGR was supplied for this configuration, so we cannot characterize this number as an improvement over any comparison condition; it should be read only as a point estimate of how much of the weak-to-strong gap the method recovers. The uncertainty is substantial relative to the estimate, and with just three seeds the sampling distribution is poorly constrained, so the interval around 0.48 is wide and the ordering against any future baseline could change. We therefore report this as a preliminary, suggestive measurement rather than evidence that the auxiliary confidence loss helps. Additional seeds and a matched baseline run at the same aux_loss_weight would be needed before drawing any directional conclusion about the method's effect.
